questions.q: You load 100 `Customer` rows and then access each customer's lazy `accounts` collection in a loop. What is this problem called?
o: The N+1 select problem
A deadlock
A phantom read
A cache stampede
questions.w: One query for customers plus one query per customer. Fix with `JOIN FETCH`, an `@EntityGraph`, batch fetching or a DTO projection.

o: Loads the association only when it is first accessed
Loads every association at application startup
Skips loading the association entirely
Caches the association for ever
questions.w: Accessing a lazy association after the session closes causes `LazyInitializationException`. Load what you need inside the transaction.

questions.q: Why is `spring.jpa.open-in-view=true` often switched off in production?
o: It holds a connection for the whole request and hides lazy loading in views
It switches lazy loading off completely for every entity
It only makes the application slower to start up
It forces every query in the request to be read-only
questions.w: Fetch what the response needs inside the service layer, then map to DTOs.

questions.q: A repository declares `List<Customer> findByLastNameAndStatus(String lastName, String status)`. How does it work?
o: Spring Data derives the query from the method name
The SQL must be written in an XML file
Every row is loaded and filtered in memory
The method does not compile
questions.w: For complex queries use `@Query` (JPQL or native) or the Criteria API/Specifications.

questions.q: What does an entity in the managed state mean for `EntityManager`?
o: Changes are detected and flushed to the database at commit
The entity can no longer be modified
The entity lives only in a separate cache
The entity has already been deleted
questions.w: This is dirty checking. You do not need to call `save()` again for an entity loaded in the same transaction.

questions.q: How does `@Version` help with concurrent updates?
o: Optimistic locking: the update fails if the version changed meanwhile
It locks the row until the transaction commits
It numbers the published versions of the REST API
It keeps a backup copy of the old row in another table
questions.w: Hibernate adds `WHERE version = ?` to the update and throws `OptimisticLockException` when no row matches. Retry or tell the user.

questions.q: Why prefer a DTO projection over returning entities from a REST endpoint?
o: It selects only needed columns and avoids exposing internals
Entities can never be serialised to JSON by any library
DTOs are quicker for developers to type than entities
Entities never contain any data when they are loaded
questions.w: Entities have lazy proxies and bidirectional links that cause recursion or leaks. DTOs give a stable API shape.

questions.q: What does `@Transactional(readOnly = true)` on a query method help with?
o: Hibernate can skip dirty checking, and reads may go to a replica
It forbids every read operation inside the method
It blocks all other transactions until it finishes
It turns on the second-level cache for the whole entity
questions.w: It is a hint, not a guarantee. It is commonly used on service methods that only read.
